help.page_title: Help - spot price, taxes, install the app and open API
help.info_intro: Learn about hourly prices, variable prices, taxes, and fees under each respective category below.
help.spot_p1: The spot price is the price your electricity trading company has to pay for the electricity. This number is often the one shown in various comparisons, newspaper articles, etc.
help.spot_p2: Spot price does not include any surcharges and VAT.
help.hourly_p: With an hourly (or, since October 2025, quarter-hourly) price you pay for your consumption interval by interval. This allows you to use less electricity during expensive periods and more electricity during cheap periods. It's a good choice for those who can move large consumers to times when electricity is cheap.
help.monthly_p: The variable monthly price works much like the hourly price, but your consumption is summed up to a monthly total, which is multiplied by the electricity company's variable price determined at the end of the month. It is not a straight average of all prices, but weighted against the consumption of all customers.
help.taxes_p: On top of the spot price you normally pay a surcharge to your electricity trading company, energy tax, grid fees and VAT. On this page, you can choose between actual price and spot price using the cogwheel in the top right corner.
help.calc_intro: The default setting displays the spot prices of electricity. You can customize how prices are shown:
help.calc_step1: Click the cogwheel icon in the top right corner.
help.multiplier_desc: Used when the electricity company has an added fee in percentage per kilowatt hour. For example, use 1.02 if there's an added fee of 2% per kWh.
help.fees_desc: Any fixed addition per kWh, in the chosen currency, before VAT.
help.factor_desc: Typically VAT. For instance, use 1.25 for a 25% VAT.
help.formula_intro: Once you've set your parameters, prices are calculated as:
help.example: Example: a spot price of 1.00 SEK/kWh, multiplier 1.02, fees 0.10 SEK and factor 1.25 gives ((1.00 × 1.02) + 0.10) × 1.25 = 1.40 SEK/kWh.
help.stored: All settings are stored in your browser only.
help.app_intro: This site is available as an app (PWA) for Windows, Android and Apple devices.
help.win_1: At the right of the address bar, click Install.
help.android_1: Tap Install, or use the three-dot menu and choose "Install app".
help.api_intro: All data is available as JSON, free of charge and without API key:
help.api_spot: prices in currency/MWh grouped by hourly (raw intervals), daily, weekly, monthly, yearly or total. Optional interval=PT15M|PT60M selects an exact resolution. One request covers at most 31 days for hourly and 366 days for daily; longer groupings are not limited.
help.api_cheapest: the cheapest unbroken period of hours from now to the end of tomorrow, for automations. consecutive=false picks the cheapest separate intervals instead, and from/to limit the search. active is true while one of the chosen intervals is in progress.
help.api_flows: net physical flow per border right now (MW).
help.api_source: Source of the data: ENTSO-E Transparency Platform, prices converted with ECB reference rates. Please mention the source when you re-use the data. Re-use is subject to the ENTSO-E Transparency Platform terms of use. spotweb is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by ENTSO-E.
help.description: How spot, hourly and variable electricity prices work, how actual prices with fees and VAT are calculated, how to install the app, and the free open JSON API.
help.api_more: Full documentation of the API, its terms of use and how the data is converted is on the API page.

api.page_title: Open API - electricity spot prices as JSON
api.description: Documentation of the free JSON API for electricity spot prices: endpoints, parameters, data sources, how the data is converted and terms of use.
api.title: Open API
api.intro: All data on this site is also available as JSON over HTTP, free of charge and without an API key. CORS is open, so the API can be called directly from a web page. The Home Assistant page has a ready-made sensor configuration.
api.terms_title: Provided for personal use, without guarantees
api.terms_own_use: The API is provided as is, for personal use such as home automation, hobby projects and your own analyses. spotweb is an independent hobby project with no connection to ENTSO-E or the ECB.
api.terms_no_guarantee: There are no guarantees of uptime, availability, response times or correctness of the data. The API may be changed, rate limited or shut down without notice. Do not use it where an outage or a wrong price can cause damage, such as trading, invoicing or safety critical control, and check the prices against the original source when it matters.
api.terms_fair_use: Be considerate: cache the responses and do not fetch the same data more often than needed. Tomorrow's prices are published once a day, around 13:00 CET. Clients that send too many requests may be blocked or get 429 Too Many Requests. For heavy use, run your own instance (the source code is open) or fetch the data directly from ENTSO-E.
api.src_entsoe: Spot prices, production, consumption, cross-border flows and outages come from the ENTSO-E Transparency Platform. The spot prices are the day-ahead prices of each bidding zone, published in EUR/MWh.
api.src_ecb: Exchange rates are the euro foreign exchange reference rates of the European Central Bank (ECB), fetched once a day.
api.src_license: The ENTSO-E data is re-used under the terms of use of the ENTSO-E Transparency Platform (CC BY 4.0). Every response names the source in source, and responses with converted prices also have a note. Credit "ENTSO-E Transparency Platform" when you re-use the data, and say that it has been converted where that applies.
api.processing_intro: Unless you ask for raw prices in EUR, what you get is not exactly the figures ENTSO-E publishes. This is what spotweb does with the data:
api.proc_currency: Currency: prices in any currency other than EUR are converted from EUR/MWh with the latest ECB reference rate. This also applies to historical prices, so older prices in for example SEK can differ from what was paid at the time. Ask for EUR if you need the original values.
api.proc_units: Unit: /api/v2/spot and /api/v2/cheapest answer in currency per MWh. /api/v2/hass answers per kWh (divided by 1000), in öre with currency=ORE (multiplied by 100), with your multiplier, extra and factor applied, rounded to decimals decimals and as text.
api.proc_grouping: Averages: daily, weekly, monthly, yearly and total, and the averages in /api/v2/hass and /api/v2/cheapest, are calculated by spotweb as time-weighted averages of the interval prices, grouped in the local time of the bidding zone. min and max are the lowest and highest interval price. A supplier's monthly price is weighted by consumption and usually differs.
api.proc_resolution: Resolution: without interval, each local day uses the zone's current market resolution (15 or 60 minutes), or the finest resolution available for days before a change. With interval=PT15M or PT60M only prices stored in exactly that resolution are returned; nothing is interpolated or averaged into another resolution.
api.proc_gaps: Repeated values: ENTSO-E leaves out positions where the value does not change (curve type A03). spotweb fills them in with the previous value, so every interval has a price.
api.proc_flows: Flows: the net flow per border is calculated by spotweb from the physical flows in both directions. Flows older than 90 days are only kept as hourly averages.
api.gen_format: All endpoints answer GET requests with JSON. Parameter names are case sensitive, values such as area and currency are not.
api.gen_time: Dates (YYYY-MM-DD) are read in the local time zone of the bidding zone. Times in the responses are in UTC, either as ISO 8601 or, in /api/v2/spot, as milliseconds since 1970-01-01.
api.gen_errors: Errors are answered with HTTP status 500 and {"status": "error", "details": "…"}, for example for an unknown area or currency, missing parameters or a too long date range. In /api/v2/hass missing prices are "-".
api.gen_cache: Responses have a Cache-Control header (usually one minute for current data and one hour for history) and an ETag, so a request with If-None-Match gives 304 Not Modified when nothing has changed.
api.ep_spot: Prices for one bidding zone and period, raw or grouped. Tomorrow's prices are included once they are published.
api.p_period: hourly (raw intervals, which despite the name can be 15 minutes), daily, weekly, monthly, yearly or total.
api.p_area: code of the bidding zone, the last part of the address of a zone page, e.g. SE3, FI, DE-LU.
api.p_dates: first and last day (inclusive), YYYY-MM-DD. At most 31 days for hourly and 366 days for daily; longer groupings have no limit.
api.p_currency: optional, any ECB currency, e.g. SEK, NOK, DKK, PLN. Default EUR (not converted).
api.p_interval: optional, PT15M or PT60M. Default is the zone's current market resolution, see above.
api.ep_spot_out: Returns data with time (start of the interval or group in ms since 1970-01-01 UTC, null for total), price (average), min and max, all in currency/MWh.
api.ep_hass: Yesterday, today and tomorrow per kWh, made for the RESTful integration of Home Assistant.
api.p_hass_required: required. currency can also be ORE for öre.
api.p_hass_fees: optional. Price = ((spot price × multiplier) + extra) × factor. extra is fees per kWh in the chosen currency, factor is usually VAT (1.25 is 25 %).
api.ep_hass_more: Returns the price right now in now, the average, lowest and highest price of today, tomorrow and yesterday, and every interval in data (st start, p price). All prices are text. The Home Assistant page has a ready-made configuration.
api.ep_cheapest: The cheapest time to use electricity, for automations such as charging a car or heating water.
api.p_hours: required, number of hours, e.g. 3 or 1.5.
api.p_consecutive: optional. true (default) gives the cheapest unbroken period, false the cheapest separate intervals.
api.p_from_to: optional time range to search, by default from now (the interval in progress included) to the end of tomorrow. Accepts dates, local times like 2026-01-02T07:00 and ISO 8601 with a time zone. At most 7 days.
api.ep_cheapest_out: Returns found, start, end, the average price in currency/MWh, the unbroken periods in windows, the chosen intervals in data and active, which is true while one of the chosen intervals is in progress. Only intervals with published prices are searched.
api.ep_flows: Physical flows between bidding zones. Without parameters: the latest net flow per border (from, to, value in MW, time).
api.p_flows_scope: optional. With area=SE3 (bidding zone) or country=sv (country, as in the address of the country page) you get the net export per neighbour and hour.
api.p_flows_dates: optional first and last day, YYYY-MM-DD, by default yesterday and today. At most 31 days.
api.ep_flows_out: Per hour, net is the total net export (MW, negative is import) and flows the net export to each neighbour.
api.ep_status: version, how up to date the data is and the latest runs of the import jobs.
api.ep_healthz: 200 ok when the service and its database are running.
api.ep_healthz_data: 200 ok when prices, production and consumption are up to date, otherwise 503 with one problem per line.
api.selfhost: These endpoints only show the current state and promise nothing about future uptime. If you need guaranteed availability, run your own instance; the source code is open.

hass.page_title: Home Assistant - electricity spot price sensor
hass.intro: You can get current and historical electricity prices in Home Assistant by using the REST endpoint together with Home Assistant's RESTful integration.
hass.entity: The example configuration gives you an entity called sensor.spotprice_now, which displays the price right now. The entity also receives a number of attributes:
hass.attr_data: every price point, yesterday to tomorrow.
hass.interval_p: The API supports hourly and 15-minute data and determines the current price based on the interval. If you customize your price settings (cogwheel in the top right), the configuration is updated immediately.
hass.free_p: The service is free and open to everyone, no API key is required. It is used at your own risk, no guarantees are given.
hass.p_area: the last part of the url when browsing an area, e.g.
hass.p_extra: fees per kWh in chosen currency, before VAT, e.g.
hass.p_multiplier: multiplier for spot price before adding fees and VAT, 1.02 is a 2% surcharge.
hass.p_interval: PT15M or PT60M. Defaults to the current market resolution of the area.
hass.apex_p: An example showing how to use the configuration above with apexcharts-card to render a graph of prices today and tomorrow.
hass.apex_settings: The unit, scale and colour thresholds of the chart follow your currency and price settings. Orange and red start at a spot price of 70 and 120 EUR/MWh; adjust them to your liking.
hass.img_alt: Home Assistant chart of spot prices today and tomorrow
hass.description: Electricity spot prices in Home Assistant with the free REST API: sensor configuration, parameters for fees, VAT and currency, and an apexcharts card.
